metadata.name: checkwash
metadata.summary: Flags known patterns of weakened tests and CI checks in a Git diff.
metadata.description:
# checkwash **v0.9.0 adds the Claude Code session-start commit window, content-bound TEST_DISABLED exemptions, broader Python and JS/TS assertion readings, and clearer handling of oversized or unreadable input.** [Publication evidence](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/docs/releases/v0.9.0-publication-verification.md) · [Release evidence and known limits](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/docs/releases/v0.9.0-public-launch.md). A pass does not prove correctness; retain exit 2 and diagnostics as analysis errors. With `--format hook-json` (the Claude Code Stop hook) an engine error now exits 0 with a "not analysed" message. The recommended Action is pinned to the same v0.9.0 release. The #419 opaque-change refusal is turned off in that published v0.9.0 pin. A no-op opaque production edit can still leave affected oracle findings at warn; #419 remains open. Read the [versioned known issues](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/v0.9.0/docs/KNOWN-ISSUES-v0.9.0.md) before relying on a pass. **Development snapshots:** the source in this checkout may be newer than the published CLI. [The advertised-release manifest](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/release/advertised.toml) records the version, commit and download bytes behind the installation commands below. New changes require their own candidate evidence and remain unreleased until the publication record verifies them; candidate CI success does not mean that the recommended Action pin includes them. [![CI](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/checkwash.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/checkwash/) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0-blue.svg)](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/LICENSE) **Check whether a code change weakens your tests.** A test can pass after it stops checking something useful. checkwash reads your Git diff and flags known patterns such as deleted assertions, skipped tests, relaxed expectations, and CI checks that stop failing. ```diff - assert total == 105.3 + assert total > 0 ``` The new assertion accepts many incorrect totals. checkwash can flag changes like this for review, including changes written by coding agents. **Runs locally. No LLM. No network during analysis. Never executes your code.** **v0.3.0 replaces five file-wide exemption rules with content-bound ones.** In v0.2.13 those rules could reuse a recorded approval for a later change to the same path; v0.3.0 retires their path-only keys. The [upgrade notes](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/docs/remediation-upgrade.md) describe the content-bound replacement, retired keys, and installation fixes. **v0.4.0 extends detection of runtime suppression, collection changes, expectation rewrites and substituted subjects, and recognizes more table refactors.** The proofs retain input identity, execution context and conservative handling of unknown code. [Release evidence and remaining limits](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/docs/releases/v0.4.0-public-launch.md) **v0.4.1 repairs Node assertion recognition ([#164](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/issues/164))** and covers Node test-file names, bounded import aliases and lexical shadows. Coverage warnings expose known assertion candidates the scanner cannot represent; they do not prove complete JS/TS coverage. The same assertion contract checks the source, wheel and zipapp. [v0.4.1 evidence and limits](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/docs/releases/v0.4.1-public-launch.md) **v0.4.2 strengthens JS/TS assertion evidence.** Test callbacks own their assertions; changing a scalar expected value or loosening positive `toBeCloseTo` precision reaches the existing detectors. Equivalent scalar spellings remain equivalent across subject checks. This is bounded syntax support, not general JS/TS analysis. [v0.4.2 evidence and limits](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/docs/releases/v0.4.2-public-launch.md) **v0.5.0 closes a round of red-team reports (#172–#181).** A skip in a fixture or setup the test runs, a selector over edited tests, a package manifest's test command, Jest's `__tests__/` layout, JS block-level and imperative skips, JS module mocks, hand-rolled JS tolerances, chai assertions and CI control flow that stops a runner now reach the detectors; #173, #180 and #181 are closed in part. Some existing findings now carry a different fingerprint, so allowlist entries for those shapes must be re-recorded; the JSON shape is unchanged. [v0.5.0 evidence and limits](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/docs/releases/v0.5.0-public-launch.md) **v0.6.0 works through the reports and rulings that followed (#196–#261).** JS/TS assertions keep their meaning across Jest, chai, Vitest and node:test, and the runner a file's imports name decides whether a moved test still runs and what a focus stops. Hand-rolled tolerances in both frontends, pytest selectors under explicit targets, skip guards in a body, a setup or a conftest hook, every `pytestmark` spelling and a CI config the reader cannot read now reach the detectors. Some existing findings now carry a different fingerprint, so allowlist entries for those shapes must be re-recorded; the JSON shape is unchanged. [v0.6.0 evidence and limits](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/docs/releases/v0.6.0-public-launch.md) **v0.9.0 makes assertion-level exemptions content-bound ([#421](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/issues/421)).** Through v0.8.0, an exemption for one rewrite of an assertion also allowed every later rewrite of the same line. Nine assertion-level rules now key a finding by the old and the new assertion as well, TEST_DISABLED keys one by what the change disabled ([#512](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/issues/512)), and their old keys stop matching: re-review and re-record those entries. [Assertion-level notes](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/docs/remediation-upgrade.md#assertion-level-rules-next-minor-421) ## Try it You need **Python 3.11+ and Git**. Download and try the offline examples first. Windows PowerShell (including 5.1): ```powershell curl.exe -LO https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/releases/download/v0.9.0/checkwash.pyz python checkwash.pyz --version python checkwash.pyz demo ``` PowerShell 5.1 aliases `curl` to `Invoke-WebRequest`; use `curl.exe` as written. macOS/Linux or Git Bash: ```bash curl -LO https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/releases/download/v0.9.0/checkwash.pyz python checkwash.pyz --version python checkwash.pyz demo ``` Then, from the root of a repository with at least two commits: ```bash python checkwash.pyz check HEAD~1..HEAD ``` This checks your last commit. Start with a change you already understand. You can also [download the file in your browser](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/releases/download/v0.9.0/checkwash.pyz). For uncommitted changes use `python checkwash.pyz check`. For a branch review, use `python checkwash.pyz check BASE...HEAD` to compare from the merge base; `BASE..HEAD` compares the two named snapshots directly. From a subdirectory, `check` analyses the whole repository from its Git root and says so in one line on stderr (since v0.8.0, [#416](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/issues/416)). Before v0.8.0, run it from the repository root. | Result | What to do | |---|---| | **Pass · exit 0** | No finding requires blocking under your configuration. Keep running your normal tests and review. | | **Block · exit 1** | Read the finding and the diff. It may be weakened verification or a false positive. | | **Error · exit 2** | Resolve the input or analysis error before relying on the result. | The default threshold is **high**: a visible **warn** can still pass. `REPAIR_EVIDENCE` describes related changes in the same diff; it does not prove a repair is correct. For JSON/SARIF output and more examples, see the [usage guide](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/docs/releases/v0.9.0-public-launch.md#use-it-and-preserve-the-result). ## Know the limits **v0.9.0 is alpha.** A pass does not prove that a change is correct or honest. Python is the main language supported; JS/TS support covers a limited set of test patterns. Known gaps remain. In v0.8.0, JS/TS `test.each`, `it.each` and `test.for` tables are not scanned: an assertion weakened or deleted in one, an edited row or a deleted table passes. In v0.9.0, each such table is a test unit, and its rows are read when they can be counted (an inline array or a tagged template, or a same-file `const` read only as a table). The rows of a `describe.each` table stay unread, and a table with a computed title is not a unit ([#428](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/issues/428)). Legitimate refactors can be flagged. The frozen historical corpus records **22 blocks out of 60 (36.7%)**. A separate pre-release source replay records 4/60 blocks, including 2/57 strictly qualified cases; three existing fixture errors remain. These are selected examples, not a general false-positive rate. The 0.10.0 development ledger retains 6/60 static source blocks after the [D-185 dispositions](docs/oracle-context-dispositions-0.10.0.md), including two additional known legitimate-refactor false blocks. This is a later source readback, not a rewrite of the historical runtime results or a published update. A changed file over 1,000,000 bytes is not read. An image, data file, lockfile, document or non-Python production source that large is reported on stderr and earns no repair evidence. Since v0.9.0 ([#454](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/issues/454)), `--format json` also lists it under `unread`, SARIF names it in a tool execution notification, and the term report adds a `!` line and, when there is no finding, opens with "analysis incomplete"; the Stop hook's JSON and `--emit-ir` do not name it. A file a detector must read (test, conftest, CI, guardrail, snapshot, JS setup, runner script or test-command file) that large stops the run with exit 2, naming it. So do a `.py` module that large, whether added, deleted, renamed or edited, and a pytest configuration file (`pytest.ini`, `.pytest.ini`, `pytest.toml`, `.pytest.toml`, `tox.ini`, `setup.cfg`, `pyproject.toml`) at any depth: either can change the module a test's import resolves to. So do any non-generated file under the root `scripts/` directory, read for the pytest commands it runs, and any other changed file that large the analysis needs as context. A shell shebang gives a file the shape of a runner script, whatever its name, except a `.py` module or a JS/TS test file. Since v0.9.0 ([#455](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/issues/455)), checkwash reads the first 200 bytes of a side over the limit to tell, and uses them for nothing else; a Git side is streamed and checked against its object id. Where those bytes are read, a file that large whose side starts with a shell shebang stops the run, naming that side, whatever its suffix (a `.py` module or a JS/TS test file that large stops the run anyway, by its own rule). A file with no extension (a dotfile such as `.envrc` counts) without one, such as a `README` or a `LICENSE`, is set aside like any document, unless another rule above makes it one a detector must read. v0.8.0 reads no byte of such a side, so every file with no extension that large stops the run there. In v0.9.0 a Git side over 64,000,000 bytes is not streamed, so its first bytes are not known: a file with no extension still stops the run when one of its Git sides is that large, and a suffixed file whose shebang is only on such a side is still set aside. When a file that large stops the run, since v0.9.0 `--format json` prints `{"unread": [...]}` on stdout instead of nothing: one `unread` entry, for the side the run refused. It is not a findings document, and term and SARIF output stay empty. With a range, json output stays empty too when the refused file is a symlinked pytest configuration's target that no detector must read. Generated output (`build/`, `dist/`, `node_modules/` and the like) is set aside like a production source unless it is a Python module, a pytest configuration, a CI file, a runner script or a file with no extension whose shebang is not known. A root `poetry.lock` or `uv.lock` that large at the base is skipped with a note on stderr, and the skip is not listed under `unread`; when the diff also changes that lockfile, the change's sides over the limit are listed like any other. A root `pyproject.toml` or `requirements*.txt` that large at the base stops every run, naming it: term, json and SARIF output exit 2 and name it on stderr only. The Claude Code Stop hook (`--format hook-json`) reports an engine error, this one included, as a non-blocking "not analysed" message on stdout that quotes the error, and exits 0. Since v0.9.0, when the run stops on a file the hook's diff changes and that file's working-tree side is over the limit, the hook blocks the stop instead, naming the file and asking to shrink, split or revert it ([#456](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/issues/456)). A file whose base side alone is over the limit, a root manifest over it at the base, and a padded file committed before the stop keep the message; the full list is in [subject integrity](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/docs/subject-integrity.md). Try it on your own changes before making it required. [Coverage and limitations](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/docs/stability.md#coverage-and-adoption-cost) · [Known gaps](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/docs/adversarial-catalog-2026-09.md) ## Use it in CI To stop a merge, make the **`checkwash` status check required** in your repository's branch rules. Installing the tool or adding a workflow alone does not enforce its verdict. The recommended Action and the CLI above are both **v0.9.0**. Record which version you use. [Full setup and exemptions](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/docs/enterprise.md) **Advisory: Action trust boundary.** Every published Action release up to and including v0.7.0 runs `python -m pip` and then `checkwash` with the pull request's checkout as the working directory, so a module in that checkout (for example a top-level `pip` package) can replace the installer and then the checker, and the pull request can tamper with the result it is judged by. Under checkwash's threat model that applies to every pull request it judges. v0.8.0 fixes it ([#372](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/pull/372)); pin the v0.9.0 Action below. If you stay on v0.7.0 or earlier, treat a pass as advisory, review the pull request before merging and keep `comment-pr` off. [Known issue](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/SECURITY.md#known-issue-action-trust-boundary)
Copy the GitHub Actions workflow and require the check Save this as `.github/workflows/checkwash.yml`: ```yaml # .github/workflows/checkwash.yml on: [pull_request] permissions: contents: read jobs: checkwash: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1 with: fetch-depth: 0 persist-credentials: false - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0 with: python-version: "3.12" - uses: taipei49314/checkwash/action@d6eda4f695fabb8e7d138f7a87b099d2028f0294 # v0.9.0 ``` After the workflow runs, open **Settings → Rules → Rulesets** and require the `checkwash` status context. Keep the job unconditional. If you administer the repository and have this project's ruleset file, you can instead create the rule with: ```bash gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/rulesets --method POST --input action/required-ruleset.json ``` This adds a ruleset; it does not replace existing ones. `checkwash doctor` can inspect the local workflow, but cannot verify live branch protection. **Why is the pin added after the release?** A release cannot embed its own commit SHA, so a release commit carries the prior release's pin; once a release's publication is verified, a follow-up on main recommends that release's own peeled commit. The recommended v0.9.0 Action includes the engine published on 2026-10-23 Asia/Taipei. A CLI upgrade does not update an existing Action. To verify another trusted release, use `git rev-parse 'vX.Y.Z^{commit}'`. [Action reference](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/action/README.md)
## More options and evidence
Install as a CLI or try the included examples If you already use pipx, install the fixed version: ```bash pipx install checkwash==0.9.0 # or from the release tag: pipx install git+https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash@v0.9.0 checkwash check HEAD~1..HEAD checkwash demo # 8 real tampering cases, blocked, offline ``` `checkwash demo` replays eight real tampering cases and one honest fix. It illustrates known patterns; it is not a coverage guarantee. You can run the same examples with `python checkwash.pyz demo`.
Read the measurements and their limits The historical six-repo sweep recorded **46 / 1800 = 2.56%** blocks: **31 false positives (1.72%)**, 15 legitimate policy blocks (0.83%). The tracked artifacts record engine **v0.3.0** (the release commit, swept 2026-09-07) on a corpus used to tune the detectors, not a held-out result. **1.33% of the corpus (24/1800) records opaque production changes**. That flag does not establish that each verdict changed or each diff was unanalyzed. Review methods vary: the three-rater agreement study covers an older 35-diff cohort, not all 46 blocks. The dedicated **22/60 refactor** result (`benchmarks/refactors/results-latest.json`, a dated v0.3.1 snapshot) is a separate population; the general-commit rate does not predict it. [Measurements and source data](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/benchmarks/README.md) · [Generated results](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/benchmarks/RESULTS.md) · [Failure ledger](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/benchmarks/FAILURES.md)

Zero runtime dependencies. [Apache-2.0](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/LICENSE).
